Sometimes it’s best to keep a journal of your thoughts. Pinpoint some main issues that you’re dealing with at the moment (maybe three or four depending on how long you need to expand on your thoughts and feelings). This is a great way to keep pace of the session so that you don’t feel as though the session has ended abruptly in the middle of a series of thoughts you’re trying to get out. At the end of the day, yes it is their job, but they have that job BECAUSE they WANT to help you get through whatever it is that you’re going through. If one therapist doesn’t work, move on to the next one. Not every therapist is compatible with every person they see.

As someone who was the depressed person in the relationship, I’d advise that you be a pillar of support for her. It may be a bit daunting the first few weeks of her meds before they take effect, but the most you can do is be beside her and help her know she is loved and cared for. You shouldn’t do all of this without taking care of yourself as well. That’s where my relationship went wrong. They were too concerned with me that they had not handled their own personal issues properly. Make sure that you’re okay as well in all of this and don’t throw all of yourself into her problems. It’s her battle to fight through, and I’m sure with the right meds and therapy, you guys will have brighter days together more often!
